spec_match.rationale: The page's claim — Safe Browsing verdicts are deliberately not web-exposed — is the feature's actual page-facing contract (no IDL exists; blink_components is UI>Browser>SafeBrowsing), and it locates where the state really lives (security_state, VerdictReceived histogram) with sources.

interactive.rationale: A run button executes five live probes in the visitor's browser and renders the browser's actual returned value per surface — the reported values are real evaluations, never assumptions.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index promises live falsifiable probes of what page JS can and cannot observe; that is precisely the page.

edge_cases.rationale: Every probe has a real failure branch (a surface appearing flips its row to 'EXPOSED — contract changed!' and the status text stops claiming full absence); probe exceptions are caught and displayed rather than swallowed.

references.rationale: Links the chromestatus entry and chrome_security_state_util.cc; cross-links the Field Verification Lab for user-level observability.

conformance.rationale: The two automatable assertions in the feature suite (no-web-exposed-verdict-api, no-warning-dom-event) are exactly this concept's probes and pass live in the shared support panel; the absence checks would genuinely fail if Chrome exposed the surfaces.

runtime_evidence.rationale: CDP harness verified the run: 5 rows rendered, status reports 5/5 absent, all badges read 'not web-exposed', zero console errors; observability-probe-{desktop,mobile}.png capture the post-run table.

telemetry_health.rationale: ssw-probe-no-web-exposure asserts the aggregate result with per-run counts after every click; a future exposure regression would surface as an assert failure in demo telemetry.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables throughout; badge pairs (emerald/rose on ivory-white backgrounds with bg-ivory text on accent) meet AA; the results table scrolls inside its own overflow-x container on narrow viewports.

accessibility.rationale: Semantic table with scoped headers and an aria-label, aria-live status output announcing run results, single keyboard-operable button with visible focus.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: 0px horizontal overflow measured at both classes post-interaction (the wide table scrolls internally); screenshots show legible type and an unclipped layout on 360x740 and 1280x800.

openQuestions.title: Re-audit the probed surface list against future Chrome releases
openQuestions.detail: The probe set covers today's plausible exposure points (navigator/window namespaces, page-visible chrome object, DOM event handler slots). If Chromium ever proposes a web-facing Safe Browsing surface under a different name, add it to the probe list so the absence claim stays complete.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible data table live status results screen reader
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use real table semantics with header scope and announce asynchronous result updates through a polite live region.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Results render into a real table with scoped column headers and an aria-label; the summary line is an aria-live output element updated after each run.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive control panel forms without horizontal overflow mobile
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Wide content must scroll inside its own container instead of forcing page-level horizontal overflow.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The probe table sits in a .table-wrap with overflow-x:auto and a min-width, keeping documentElement.scrollWidth equal to the viewport on mobile.

summary: Inspection concept: turns the feature's privacy design (verdicts invisible to pages) into five live, falsifiable probes that print the browser's actual values, with an explicit failure presentation if any surface ever appears. Harness-verified: 3/3 probe checks, 0 console errors, table scrolls internally on mobile.
